note: GA-010: a release lane is decided by what the change touches, by code, at the reviewed head. The most restrictive lane any path or effect matches wins. closed never opens on its own under DR-113. A repository may replace this table whole with .gstack/release-lanes.json; the two are never merged.

closed.purpose: Changes that touch money, migrations, credentials, the agent's identity, workflows, rulesets, ownership, how git reads the tree, or this table itself. DR-113 does not apply (GA-010).

wide.purpose: Shared code and changes many files name: the agent merges only with the ledger clear, coverage checked, links verified and no open unknown needing the repository (GA-010).

light.note: XE-049.7: every changed path must match one of these, as the key says (existing_paths: modified, not added; version_only: only version fields change; status_only: only item **Status:** lines change; an Amendments-log line never). Never a CODEOWNERS path, .github/ or a hooks/ directory. No cross-vendor review: tests green and the check ledger clear, and the agent merges.
light.purpose: Docs, existing tests, version fields and status lines: merged on green tests and a clear check ledger with no cross-vendor review (XE-049.7).

owned.purpose: GA-008: what CI runs to gate main, every hooks directory, the scorer's dependency files, what sets the agent's token and data permissions, and the spend cap.
GO-001: a goal's brief, plan, tests and run record change only with his approval.
GO-011.9: the first two successors of a goal carry no owner; goal_successor.py, run in the required tests check, holds them.
GO-011.9: the script that holds the unowned successors.
GO-011.2: a goal's own goal-runs/<id>/ is not owned; the folder's README is.

GA-013: how git reads the tree (root .gitattributes and .gitmodules; anchored, because goal_ready refuses an unanchored pattern, and the closed lane covers a nested .gitattributes) and this policy table, in both its homes.
